task_specification.objective: Close the player-facing upgrade hierarchy defect first, then secure the authored arena spatial contract while preserving the mature dense-profile protocol for native 1920x1080 qualification by Tester/GameLoop Runtime.

diagnosis.root_cause: The upgrade presenter bounds projected changes upstream, but its active _rebuild_stat_rows sink still trusts an unbounded array and can render more than three rows. Dense qualification has a different, external cause: the candidate already exposes the three-cycle profile protocol, but llvmpipe cannot supply qualifying native-renderer samples. The authored cemetery also needs same-loop runtime confirmation that its existing package-bound expansion, external depth, landmark collision, visibility margins, and perimeter remain aligned.

stop_conditions: Do not begin dense/world work until the real upgrade-draft scene and render sink have been repaired and focused code checks pass.
If dense recapture still reports a software renderer, stop candidate-side profiling edits; preserve the existing receipts and carry qualification to a native environment.
Do not replace, duplicate, split, or modify children of the preserved authored cemetery package, Warden Lantern, Gravespade, or Wandering Wisps assets.
Do not turn external recapture, formal review, issue closure, or deferred ordinary-route/MCP findings into Developer implementation work.

Stop world expansion if it would require proxy roads, floor patches, facade slices, or a second environment package; use the intact authored package plus product-owned datum, collision, navigation, spawn, and objective bindings.

strategy.rationale: Use two distinct root-cause treatments. Enforce the three-delta rule at the final UI render sink and exercise the complete choice interface. For the repeatedly treated dense issue, avoid another collector/instrumentation rewrite: advance the required arena capability around the preserved authored map, audit the already-present profile contract, and leave native qualification to the environment that can produce valid samples.

code: Run focused parser/resource checks for scripts/ui/upgrade_draft.gd, its scene/controller bindings, and the direct over-cap render-sink fixture.
Run the dense-profile self-audit and verify prepare/advance/reset actions remain editor-only, absent from release exports, and report the immutable contract signature.
Run the frozen native Godot project and host boot checks; reject new parser, resource-load, freed-instance, signal, input-action, or recurring runtime errors.
runtime: Tester opens a native upgrade draft with an over-cap projection and compares rendered rows with authoritative offer/selection state for keyboard, mouse, and gamepad input; verify one commit and observable post-choice combat behavior.

Tester performs an ordinary movement replay from spawn through the cross-route, around the central mausoleum, to each boundary/perimeter, checking player position, collision contacts, landmark visibility, camera coverage, and world bounds.

GameLoop Runtime and Tester—not Developer—recapture three serial tester_dense_prepare, tester_dense_advance, tester_dense_reset cycles on a native 1920x1080 hardware renderer with 25–40 enemies, boss behavior, three weapons, pickups, animation, VFX, lights, UI, and audio.

For each dense cycle, bind renderer classification, viewport, cycle/setup/advance generations, requested/resolved density, frame/physics/render distributions, high-water marks, subsystem samples, runtime errors, lifecycle deltas, reset isolation, and next-frame input context. Tester owns the verdict and issue closure.
visual: Capture the upgrade page at 1920x1080 plus representative windowed/UI-scale states: default keyboard focus, mouse hover/press, gamepad focus, newly unlocked weapon, unavailable choice, and selected confirmation.

Capture separated world views at spawn, the central building from approach and side traversal, four cardinal directions, and the boundary/perimeter; confirm coherent external depth, aligned collision, stable landmark visibility, and no void or proxy-floor exposure.

Capture representative dense gameplay from the shipped high-angle camera during the qualified sample window, confirming readable crowd density and unchanged authored cemetery composition without profiling HUD clutter.

done_when: The active _rebuild_stat_rows sink independently renders at most three decision-relevant rows even when called directly with four or more projected changes; the cap does not rely only on scene metadata or upstream normalization.

Each offered choice leads with an authored weapon or upgrade silhouette/icon, followed by compact stat icons and aligned, truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant deltas.
NEW, LOCKED, UNAVAILABLE, UNKNOWN, N/A, or equivalent placeholder text never appears in the CURRENT value column; unchanged, zero-placeholder, unrelated, and exhaustive rows are omitted.

Names, rank/eligibility state, and one restrained consequence line remain subordinate to the visual hierarchy and reflow without clipping at 1920x1080, supported windowed sizes, and supported UI scales.
Keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus, hover, pressed, unavailable, newly unlocked, and selected states are visibly distinct without resizing cards or obscuring tradeoffs.

Held confirm applies exactly one authoritative choice, the selected id/rank/modifier is reflected in runtime state before gameplay resumes, and the next relevant combat event reflects the applied upgrade.
tasks.instructions: Work first in the real upgrade-draft presenter and scene. Add a final sink-side MAX_DECISION_DELTAS guard inside _rebuild_stat_rows so every caller is bounded, then retain the existing upstream filtering as defense in depth. Add or extend a focused fixture that passes more than three projected changes directly to the sink and covers placeholder, unchanged, and new-weapon cases. Preserve the icon-led moonlit gold/teal presentation, current weapon silhouettes, fixed three-card composition, authoritative controller transaction, and complete keyboard/mouse/gamepad interaction. Do not broaden this task into other shell pages.
tasks.title: Enforce the upgrade draft's three-delta render-sink contract

done_when: The intact authored cemetery remains one authoritative environment instance, and its native streets provide a larger traversable scale with a readable loop and cross-route; candidate-owned collision, navigation, spawn, and objective anchors agree with rendered geometry.

A coherent non-playable external world or external depth surrounds the playable datum from spawn, four cardinal views, and the perimeter without visible void, proxy-floor dominance, or an abrupt map edge.

The central building/mausoleum landmark has collision aligned to its rendered footprint: ordinary movement and a movement replay cannot pass through it, snag on a materially oversized invisible barrier, or enter its interior.

The central landmark and other prominent map surfaces show no disappearance or camera occlusion drift during ordinary movement from spawn, across the cross-route, around the landmark, and along the boundary/perimeter.

Every boundary blocks the Warden consistently while remaining visually legible, and spawn lanes remain outside the protected camera area, inside authored world bounds, and connected to playable space.

The existing dense-profile contract remains editor-only and unchanged unless a new candidate defect is demonstrated; it exposes 25–40-enemy setup, all three weapon families, boss, pickups, animation, VFX, lights, UI and audio, bounded work/high-water metrics, runtime errors, lifecycle deltas, setup/cycle generations, and reset isolation.

On a qualifying native 1920x1080 renderer, three serial prepare/advance/reset cycles produce distinct complete receipts, non-empty frame/physics/render distributions, stable high-water behavior, and no growth in live actors, pooled objects, callbacks, timers, audio, pause ownership, or input actions across Retry.
tasks.instructions: After completing the upgrade task, inspect the existing authored-world bindings from rendered package bounds through the outer datum. Correct only candidate-owned wrapper/datum, collision, navigation metadata, spawn, objective, visibility-margin, camera, and perimeter integration needed to preserve the expanded playable envelope and external depth. Keep the complete authored cemetery package intact; do not move or edit imported child meshes or introduce replacement roads, patches, landmarks, or environment families. Exercise the central mausoleum collision and culling contract through ordinary movement. For dense qualification, run the existing contract self-audit and source guards but do not add another telemetry treatment merely because the current environment is llvmpipe; any native three-cycle recapture belongs in validation.
